judgment_calls: UseReceiveEngineParams.createEngine is a FACTORY (() => ReceiveEngine), not a pre-built engine instance -- the effect calls createEngine() fresh on every mount, sidestepping receive-engine.ts's 'start() only from lifecycle uninitialized' guard under a React 18 Strict-Mode dev double-invoke. See architecture.json judgment_calls.fresh-engine-per-mount-via-factory and post-impl VQ-S8-009.

Full buildProjection is run once at every hook mount (seeded from persistence.loadAcceptedEvents + replayOrder), treating every mount as Implementation Constraint 7's 'restart' case, not only origin:'restored' starts -- see architecture.json judgment_calls.mount-time-persistence-seed-is-the-restart-case and post-impl VQ-S8-011.

Two small shared test-infrastructure additions were required outside scope.includes' three files, both necessary prerequisites for the mandated .test.tsx file to run at all in this repo (its first .tsx test file): vitest.config.ts gained `oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } }` (Vite 8's oxc transform otherwise inherits tsconfig.json's Next.js-recommended 'jsx: preserve' and refuses to parse JSX), and package.json/package-lock.json gained react-test-renderer pinned to the EXACT installed react/react-dom version (19.2.4, not a caret range) plus @types/react-test-renderer as devDependencies -- react-test-renderer enforces an exact internal-version match with react at runtime, not just a semver-compatible peer range. See post-impl VQ-S8-010.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: This repo had zero prior .tsx test infrastructure, so two test-runner gaps had to be diagnosed from scratch before the hook's own logic could be exercised: (1) Vite 8's default oxc transform silently inherits tsconfig.json's 'jsx: preserve' and fails to parse any JSX with an opaque error, requiring a scoped `oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } }` override in vitest.config.ts; (2) react-test-renderer requires an EXACT react-version match at runtime (a caret-range peerDependency is not sufficient to avoid a runtime crash), requiring `npm view` reconnaissance to find and pin the one published version (19.2.4) matching the installed react/react-dom exactly. Neither is discoverable from the story spec or architecture.md.
retrospective.surprised_by: react-test-renderer's initial render of a hook-bearing component is silently deferred past the synchronous portion of even an `act(async () => {...})` callback -- a straightforward `await act(async () => { create(<Harness/>); await vi.waitFor(() => expect(state).toBe(...)) })` throws on an undefined hook-state read because the component hasn't actually rendered yet when the first `vi.waitFor` poll runs. A manual real-timer flush-and-retry loop (`waitUntil`), re-entering `act()` on every attempt, was the only pattern found to reliably observe post-mount asynchronous engine state without spurious 'not wrapped in act(...)' warnings.
